result:
The fix is recorded by changeset `flat-mammals-fail.md` (O3-6093, "Improve support for arrow functions in expression variable extractor"), which patches `@openmrs/esm-expression-evaluator` and `@openmrs/esm-framework`. The code change is in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-expression-evaluator/src/extractor.ts`:

- **`visitArrowFunctionExpression`** copies the enclosing `boundNames`, adds the arrow's identifier parameters, and visits the body with that extended set. This is what keeps `x` out of the results for `a.map(x => f(b))` while still walking the body, so `f` and `b` are reported.
- **`visitIdentifier`** reports a name only if it is not a global and not in `context.boundNames`. Before the fix, the arrow body was not visited with the parameter set, so nested identifiers were lost.
- **`EvaluationContext.boundNames`** and its initialisation in `createContextInternal` hold the parameter scope.
- **`visitExpression`** dispatches `ArrowFunctionExpression` to the visitor above.

The regression tests in `extractor.test.ts` cover the fix: body identifiers in arrow functions (lines 50–57), parameter exclusion including nested arrows (59–64), and parameter scoping to the arrow body only (66–68).

I did not find a commit SHA or PR number for the change. The only indexed mention of O3-6093 is the changeset, and I had no commit-listing tool available to search history. The consumer `openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib` calls `extractVariableNames` but was not changed for this fix.
